To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
information disclosure, CEO characteristics and firm characteristics are important factors affecting buyback completion rates.

1) information disclosure and CEO characteristics (overconfidence and CEO tenure) affect buyback completion rate; 2) large and widely held companies that have a past buy back completion record are more likely to successfully complete buyback programs; 3) the buyback completion rate is positively related to subsequent buyback programs.
the share buyback announcement and completion rates are higher in firms with more information disclosure and in firms with overconfident CEOs.

the share buyback market is not a mere financial engineering tool, and firms that disclose information and exhibit CEO overconfidence are more likely to successfully complete buybacks.
